trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External party submitting transactions (L1 user or L2 sequencer). No authentication required for L1 submissions. All transaction data must be fully validated including type bytes, signatures, and content.

trusted_external_entities.name: L2 Rollup
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Layer 2 rollup system defining RIP transaction types. While rollups have some protocol-level authentication via challenge mechanisms, the transaction type definitions and data must still be validated against namespace boundaries. L1 nodes should reject invalid RIP type usage.

trusted_external_entities.name: Genesis Configuration File
trusted_external_entities.rationale: File-based configuration in assets/ directory. Trust is based on deployment environment integrity - file should be verified against known checksums. A tampered genesis file could pre-allocate malicious balances or set dangerous parameters.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Browser Extension
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Browser extension that manages keys and injects EIP-1193 provider. Any browser extension can inject code into the page context. Must be treated as potentially malicious - validate provider objects, freeze objects to prevent modification, and handle SVG icons safely via img tags only.

trusted_external_entities.name: User
trusted_external_entities.rationale: End user who selects a wallet from discovered providers. Users can be tricked by phishing or social engineering. DApps cannot verify user intent or whether the user has been deceived by a malicious wallet impersonator.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Browser Extension
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Browser extension explicitly attempting to impersonate legitimate wallets or inject malicious code. Must be defensively handled via Object.freeze(), duplicate UUID detection, and safe SVG rendering.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required including EIP-2718 envelope format, transaction type namespace (0x40-0x7f for RIP), signature verification, and content validation.
Injected provider code cannot be trusted. DApps must apply defensive measures: freeze provider objects, validate UUID format, detect duplicates, and render icons safely via img tags only.
Malicious extensions will attempt prototype pollution, wallet impersonation, and SVG script injection. Mitigations include Object.freeze(), img-only SVG rendering, and duplicate UUID detection.
